t: This is the site of the Dorset Garden Theatre, a London playhouse built in 1671. It is long gone, so what you have here is history rather than a building. It was first known as the Duke of York's Theatre, or the Duke's Theatre. When the Duke became James the Second in 1685, it was renamed the Queen's Theatre, after his wife Mary of Modena, and the name stayed when William the Third and Mary the Second took the throne in 1689. The theatre was designed by Sir Christopher Wren, the architect who rebuilt so many City churches after the Great Fire.
